turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come on in and sit wherever's easiest for the back. You look wrecked, the pair of you. What's brought you in?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): The back. The lower back. It's been murder, and I'm sick of talking about it already.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's like a briar, doctor, and he's not sleeping. We moved house and he lifted every box himself.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Sheila, I can talk. It's been a few weeks. Or since the move. I can't put a date on it.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's alright. Sheila, when do you think it started?
[SEG0006] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The move was six weeks ago. He was hunched the night we shifted the couch, and I'd say it's been six weeks solid.
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah, that is not it. I was grand for a while after the move. This is a couple of weeks, not six. I'm not fighting about a couch.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): We'll leave the dates for now. Whereabouts is the pain, and what's it like when it's bad?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Low down, across the belt line. Dull, and then it grabs if I bend. Mornings are desperate.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does it go down either leg?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. Can we not pick at that.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): We'll park it. Any numbness, or pins and needles, in the legs or round the groin?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No numbness. The legs feel normal.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the waterworks. Any struggle to pass urine, any leaking, or not feeling when the bladder's full?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Bladder's the same as ever. That's not why I'm here.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Have you lost weight without trying?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Trousers are a bit slack. Not really, though. I'm just off the dinners.
[SEG0018] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He picks at his food, but he's not wasting away. Appetite's gone with the pain, that's all.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever, night sweats, or shivering?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. I'm tired, not sick-sick. Don't write me down as a temperature.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tired since when?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Since the back got bad. I'm not sleeping on it. I'm wrecked the whole day.
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's up half the night pacing the kitchen, then into the warehouse for seven. And he's been at the tablets.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, warehouse operative. On my feet, lifting all day. They haven't a light duty between them, so don't bother suggesting it.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): What tablets are you taking, and what strength?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Ibuprofen from the chemist. I nearly said the two hundred milligram, but no, it's the four hundred milligram ones. Three times a day.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you get the three doses into you, and are you taking them with food?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Mostly with food. I take them. Well, I miss the odd one, I'm not a robot.
[SEG0029] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The middle-of-the-day one, he misses that half the time. I've seen the blister pack.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): It is not half the time. The odd one. I'm sat right here, Sheila.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anything else for the pain?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Paracetamol as well, for a while. Two of the five hundred milligram tablets, four times a day. Stopped them last week. Useless.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines, or to anything else?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing I know of.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Operations in the past, or any long-term illness?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No operations. The same spot in the back gave a twinge five-ish years ago and then it settled. Nothing else ongoing.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Smoking, or drink?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't smoke. Never did, really. A few pints at the weekend normally. Not this month, I'm too sore and too tired.
[SEG0039] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's just the two of us in the house. The kids are grown and gone, so it's me keeping an eye.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm glad you're with him. I'm going to press along the low back. Say where it's worst.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): There. Right side. For God's sake, that's enough poking.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): The muscles either side of the low spine are tender, and it's clearly worse on the right. The bone itself isn't sore when I tap it.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Straight leg raise is clear on both sides, no pain shooting down. Power and feeling in the feet are normal. You can sit.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Finally. If I'm sweating it's from standing, not a fever. I already said that.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Noted. In the chair your blood pressure was one hundred and thirty-six over eighty-two, the pulse was seventy-four, and the temperature is thirty-six point six.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): I didn't come in about blood pressure. Is the back knackered or not?
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pressure's fine. This fits a mechanical strain of the low back from the lifting. That's my working impression, not a final label, until we see how it behaves.
[SEG0048] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He has himself told it's broke. Does he not need a scan, doctor?
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): I said it feels broke. I did not say it is broke. Give over, the two of you.
[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): I don't think it's broken, and no scan today. If it's not settling in six weeks, we might arrange a plain x-ray of the lumbar spine.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Six weeks. I've had enough weeks. Brilliant.

[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stay on the ibuprofen, four hundred milligrams three times a day, and take it with food every time. You can add the paracetamol back if you want, one gram four times a day, and don't go over those amounts.

[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): Keep moving, short walks, and heat is fine if it eases you. Don't stay in the bed all day, and no heavy lifting in the warehouse until this settles. I know that's easier said.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Work will love that. I'm not after a sick cert, I'm not that man. And if I lie down tonight, I'm lying down.

[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): A lie-down is fine, it's all day in the bed that seizes you up. Come back sooner if the pain shoots hard down a leg, or you go numb, or the bladder changes. If it's not better in a fortnight, book back in with me.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): A fortnight, then. I'm going home. Don't tell me to be positive about it. Thanks, I suppose.

spec.situation: Manual worker or office worker with low back pain for 'a few weeks or since the move'; doctor asks about red flags (numbness, bladder, weight loss, fever) one by one; patient answers some clearly, some vaguely or with a story. Painkiller use mentioned.
features: ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.

bad.reason: Family says it's just the two of us and grown kids gone; wife relationship not explicitly stated.

omissions.text: Pain is across the belt line, described as dull with grabbing pain on bending, and mornings are the worst.
Possible leg radiation was equivocal: patient said it sometimes goes down a leg but 'not really'.
Weight loss was asked about and not clearly present: patient said trousers are a bit slack / off his food, family member said appetite is down with pain but he is not 'wasting away'.
Night sweats and shivering were specifically asked about along with fever and effectively denied when the patient said he was 'tired, not sick-sick'.
Ibuprofen adherence detail is missing: he usually takes it with food but misses the odd dose; family member reported the middle-of-the-day dose is missed about half the time.
No heavy lifting at the warehouse was advised, but the patient stated there is no light duty available and he was not seeking a sick note.
